takeaways: Arista crushed it: $1.20 of adjusted EPS vs $1.08 expected, and $3.66 billion in revenue vs $3.33 billion (FactSet via MarketWatch). Its own guidance had been $3.3 billion.

Revenue grew 58.5% from a year ago, the fastest growth since its 2014 IPO, and 20.5% from last quarter. Arista sells the networking gear that connects AI chips inside data centers, so AI build-outs show up here fast.
It's very profitable: a 49.1% adjusted operating margin (44.9% GAAP), and GAAP net income of $1.56 billion, or $1.22 a share, nearly double last year's 67 cents.
The Q4 guide is well above the Street: $3.9-4.0 billion in revenue vs $3.6 billion expected, and $1.26-1.30 in adjusted EPS vs $1.15 (Investing.com).
Arista also launched rack-scale AI networking designs with partners including AMD, Broadcom, Meta and Microsoft, and joined the S&P 100 in September, per the release.
verdict: Arista beat its own guidance by about $360 million and then guided Q4 above where analysts had it, so the stock did a cannonball after hours. When AI companies build data centers, somebody has to sell them the cables-and-switches plumbing, and Arista is cashing those checks. Only catch: expectations just got taller too.
